reviews.headline: France - Turquie. La qualification, la première place mais un manque de maîtrise pour les Bleus
reviews.quote: Cette inefficacité a fait trembler les Bleus jusqu’en fin de match, et le but du break inscrit par Kroupi, son premier, bien servi par Cherki (2-0, 80’).
reviews.quote_en: This wastefulness made Les Bleus tremble until the end of the match, and the clinching goal came from Kroupi, his first, well set up by Cherki (2-0, 80').
reviews.point: France qualified and topped the group, but they showed the same weaknesses as in Italy: they wasted many chances, and Zidane still has plenty of work to do.

reviews.headline: Sans briller, l'équipe de France s’impose face à la Turquie et se qualifie pour les quarts de finale de la Ligue des nations
reviews.quote: Dans un match plus accroché que ce que les classements des deux équipes pouvaient laisser penser, les Bleus ont dû prendre leur mal en patience avant de faire la différence.
reviews.quote_en: In a match that was tighter than the two teams' rankings suggested, Les Bleus had to be patient before making the difference.
reviews.point: France won without shining: they dominated a tighter game than expected and had to wait for the second half, helped by an own goal and Kroupi's first international goal.

reviews.headline: Francia gana a Turquía y se clasifica para cuartos de la Liga de Naciones
reviews.quote: Pero el contenido del partido volvió a dejar mucho que desear y plantea muchas incógnitas pese al regreso del capitán Kylian Mbappé, baja en Milán por dolores en los isquiotibiales.
reviews.quote_en: But the content of the match once again left a lot to be desired and raises many questions despite the return of captain Kylian Mbappé, who missed Milan with hamstring pain.
reviews.point: France topped the group, but the wire report says the performance was again poor and leaves open questions about Zidane's possession-based approach.

title_options: Why France only won 2-1 in Bordeaux
The own goal, the late header and the 0.86 miss
script.description:
France beat Turkiye 2-1 in Bordeaux and reached the Nations League quarter-finals. They created 3.36 expected goals to Turkiye's 1.54, yet needed an own goal at minute 49 and Kroupi's strike at minute 80, and Bardakci's header at minute 90 made the ending tense. We ask how a team makes 7 big chances and wins by one goal, following Rayan Cherki, Arda Güler and Emirhan Topçu.

We use pre-match words from Zinédine Zidane (Flashscore) and Sergen Yalçın (Türkiye Today), and the match report from Ouest-France. Data: FotMob.

shots.text: France create 3.36 expected goals, or xG, and still have to survive the end of the match in Bordeaux. How does a team make 7 big chances and win by only one goal? xG is simply what the chances were worth in goals.
Minute 90. A Turkiye corner. Abdülkerim Bardakci rises and heads it in, with Arda Güler credited with the assist. It is 2-1. Ten minutes earlier, France led 2-0.

shots.text: Round 6 of the group. France arrive with 3 wins, 1 draw and 1 defeat in their last 5, the defeat a 3-1 loss in Italy three days earlier. Turkiye arrive with 5 defeats in 5.

shots.text: Three people carry this story. Rayan Cherki plays behind Kylian Mbappé in France's 4-2-3-1. Our reading: his job is to find gaps in a Turkiye back five.
Arda Güler, at 98 million euros, is Turkiye's most valuable starter. If Turkiye are to hurt France, our reading is that it runs through him.
And Emirhan Topçu, one of Turkiye's 3 centre-backs. A defender hopes for a quiet night. Keep minute 49 in mind.

shots.text: Stade Atlantique, Bordeaux. France take control of the first half, and FotMob's momentum graph has them on top for most of it. Turkiye sit in a 5-4-1.

The chances come. Minute 21, Bradley Barcola breaks away and is saved. Minute 34, Mbappé shoots and is saved too. Turkiye's one real answer comes at minute 35: İsmail Yüksek's shot, worth 0.37 xG, is saved.
Half time, 0-0. France dominate and have nothing to show for it. Remember that feeling. It comes back.

shots.text: Minute 49. A France corner leads to two chances. Adrien Rabiot's header goes wide. Then Bradley Barcola shoots from very close to goal. That chance is worth 0.86 xG, the kind that scores about 9 times in 10. He misses.
In that same minute, France take the lead anyway. The pack credits Emirhan Topçu with an own goal. It is 1-0. The numbers cannot show how it went in, only who is credited.
Our reading: this is the turning point. France finally lead, but through a goal credited to a defender, not a finisher. Topçu ends with the lowest rating of any starter, 5.6.

scenes.on_screen: The second goal, the second scare

shots.text: France lead, but the match does not close. Mbappé shoots at minutes 64, 73 and 75, and every one is saved or blocked.

Minute 80. Substitute Junior Kroupi scores in open play with his right foot. Rayan Cherki sets it up. It is 2-0. The shot is worth only 0.15 xG, and it goes in. Cherki ends as player of the match, rated 8.4.
Then France miss again. Minute 88, Lucas Da Cunha shoots from a 0.20 chance and misses. Two minutes later, Turkiye's best-rated player, Güler at 8.1, sets up Bardakci's header. 2-1.

shots.text: Here is the answer. FotMob's numbers put France's chances at 3.36 xG, but only 2 goals came, and one was an own goal. France missed 6 of their 7 big chances.
The clearest case is Barcola at minute 49. A chance worth 0.86 xG should go in.

Our reading: the margin was one goal because France's finishing was poor, not because Turkiye matched them for chances. The numbers cannot show how much was French waste and how much was Turkiye defending.

shots.text: So how does a team make 7 big chances and win by one goal? By missing 6 of them. France go through to the quarter-finals, but Ouest-France says the same wasted chances showed in Italy.
Turkiye leave Bordeaux with a late goal for Bardakci and a sixth defeat in a row. Güler, at 8.1, was good enough to lift them, but not to earn a point.
Making chances is one skill. Taking them is another. Will France's misses cost them in the quarter-finals? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to The Other Touchline.

notes: Scene 1 opens with "Minute 90. A corner for Turkiye. Arda Güler gets the assist.", a list of match events with no tension. Lead with the contrast instead: France had 3.36 xG and still needed to survive the last seconds. Make the open question the second sentence.

"So why did France have to survive the final minutes of a match they controlled? The scoreline hides the answer." is a vague tease, and it promises a mystery that Scene 7 then answers with a stat dump. Ask a sharper question, such as how a team creates 7 big chances and wins by only one goal, and answer it directly in the finale.

Scene 3 sets up three "characters" but only Cherki gets a real arc. Güler and Topçu are just named, and Topçu's "Remember his name" is a setup the script never pays off beyond the own goal. Either follow all three through the match or cut to one or two.

Scene 7 ("Data from FotMob gives France 3.36 xG... 7 big chances and missed 6... 51 touches... 20") reads like a stats report. Cut it to xG and the 6-of-7 big chances, and tie them to a specific miss such as Barcola's 0.86 chance.

Scene 8 repeats what the story has already shown: franceinfo and Ouest-France are quoted at length, each followed by "The data agrees". Trim to one short quote and move on, because the "Our verdict" line adds nothing new.

Scene 4's momentum percentage and the 7-shot first-half breakdown ("The other six are worth 0.06 xG or less each") slow the pace. Keep one line about France's pressure and the Yüksek save, and cut the rest. Scene 9's closing question ("comfortable win or a lucky one?") feels like an engagement tag, not an answer to the opening question.

shorts.title: Rayan Cherki: 8.4, the best rating on the pitch

shots.text: Rayan Cherki. 8.4, the best rating of any player in France against Turkiye.
Zidane's 4-2-3-1 placed him in the middle of the three behind Kylian Mbappé, between Olise and Barcola.
He took one shot, in minute 13, worth 0.04 expected goals. His value came from somewhere else.
Minute 80, still 1-0. Cherki set up substitute Junior Kroupi, who scored his first international goal. 2-0.

France had 7 big chances and missed 6. His pass was the one that became a goal. The pack has no passing numbers for him, so the rating is a judgement, not a count. Was 8.4 fair? Full story on the channel.

shorts.title: Minute 49: the own goal that broke Turkiye's plan

shots.text: 0-0 until minute 49. Then Emirhan Topçu put the ball into his own net.
France had been on top for 79% of the first-half minutes. Turkiye sat in a 5-4-1, and their coach had said they would defend deeper against France.
Morocco used a similar idea at the 2022 World Cup, with 38% of the ball: stay compact and wait. It works until one touch ends the wait.
Topçu was the lowest-rated starter, 5.6. The pack lists no assist and cannot show how the ball reached him.
Same minute, Barcola missed a chance worth 0.86 expected goals. Turkiye had held for 48 minutes. Was it Topçu's error, or France's pressure? Full story on the channel.
